messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Realtime alert: p99 latency breach detected for route `generate.v1` in us-west2. p95=420ms p99=2.8s over last 3m. Trigger: realtime-pulse-detector. Paging on-call @maya. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/latency?route=generate.v1
maya: Ack, I'm online. Looking at traces and canary history now. Any recent deploys to us-west2? @alex @jenny
alex: No deploys from me in last hour. I did push a small autoscaler tweak earlier today but nothing in the last 30m.
jenny: I see an increase in streaming stalls on the same route in the tail traces — a lot of GPUtil queue wait spikes. Suspect a burst of long contexts hitting a quantized model variant.
simon: I'm checking infra metrics (GPU util, NVLink errors). Quick check: no GPU OOMs reported but network retransmits up on a subset of hosts in us-west2.
maya: Ok steps: 1) verify global vs regional 2) check canary percentage 3) attempt quick mitigation (route-shift / fallback) 4) notify customers if impact persists. I'll grab the traces.
maya: Trace summary: many requests have KV cache miss pattern then long stall at decoder step, appears correlated with sequence lengths > 1024. Can we pull recent request histograms? @infra-ops
infra-ops: Pulling histograms now — sending a short query.
infra-ops: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="generate.v1",region="us-west2"}[3m])) by (le))
```
infra-ops: Result shows p99 jumped from ~700ms to 2.7s starting at 15:11 UTC, sustained across ~6 hosts.
alex: Proposing quick fallback: route-weight shift from model-quant-q4 -> model-std-fp16 for 20% of traffic, and enable prefix-KV caching for candidates. Will push a temporary route rule.
maya: Do it. Keep canary small so we don't overload fp16 hosts.
alex: Running route weight change: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/route-shift \
  -d '{"route":"generate.v1","from":"model-quant-q4","to":"model-std-fp16","percent":20,"duration":"20m"}'
```
alex: Done — 20% shifted as of 15:18 UTC.
jenny: After shift, p99 dropped to 1.1s within 90s, p95 unchanged ~430ms. Streaming stalls reduced in traces for canary traffic.
simon: Correlation: the affected hosts are on a new NIC firmware version (fw 3.4.2) rolled yesterday. I'm seeing packet drops on those hosts during high backpressure. Opening infra ticket to rollback NIC firmware on the cohort.
infra-ops: Rolling rollback request to kernel team. ETA for rollback pilot: 45m.
maya: For immediate mitigation, let's expand fallback to 40% and temporarily disable aggressive batching on quantized hosts to reduce queue depth.
alex: Expanding to 40% now and toggling batching config for model-quant-q4 nodes: ```json
{"batching":{"max_batch_size":64,"queue_timeout_ms":20}}
```
alex: Changes applied at 15:23 UTC.
jenny: Observed further p99 improvement to ~820ms. Tail stalls still slightly elevated on the worst hosts but overall customer-facing latency is improving.
maya: Great. Notify SRE on-call and comms: customers on high-throughput plans may have seen slower p99 but availability unaffected. @simon can you confirm no error-rate spike?
simon: No error-rate spike, 5xx stable. Only elevated latency. Infra rollback will be primary fix.
maya: Logging mitigation actions, will keep watch for 30m. If rollback pilot shows clean metrics we can fully shift traffic back and re-enable batching.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5001. Severity: high (SLO risk). Linked runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/latency-runbook
alex: I'll prepare a temporary dashboard snapshot and a short post-incident note. If anyone sees p99 climb again, escalate to full page.
jenny: Also capturing representative traces for evals team to see model sensitivity to long sequences on quantized runtime.
maya: Thanks team — continuing watch. I'll update if anything changes. Next update target +10m. :eyes:
infra-ops: Rolling metrics: p95=440ms p99=880ms at 15:31 UTC. Keeping rollback in flight.
simon: Infra pilot rollback started at 15:37 UTC.
infra-ops: Pilot rollback successful on 3 hosts; p99 on those dropped to ~450ms. Starting staggered rollback on remaining cohort.
maya: If rollback completes cleanly, we'll de-escalate and convert to follow-up postmortem. For now keep incident channel open.
alex: Noted — saving logs and route change commands to INC-2026-5001 thread.
jenny: Quick note for comms: recommend telling customers we mitigated by shifting to a more stable model variant and rolling back a NIC firmware causing packet drops; no data loss.
maya: Closing initial triage stage. Will handoff to postmortem owners after rollback completes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
